channel.title: Potomac Local News - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Potomac Local News (potomaclocal.com)

item.title: Prince William Skater Stumbles In Free Skate
item.description: Prince William County athletes are making headlines at the 2026 Milano Cortina Winter Olympics, with gold medals, tough finishes, and final runs still ahead.

item.title: Opinion: If Schools Can’t Keep Students on Campus, What Are We Doing?
item.description: Parents in Prince William County have worked hard to get their children back into classrooms after the disruption and damage of COVID-19. They’ve listened to school leaders. They’ve responded to calls for better attendance. They’ve adjusted work schedules, transportation routines, and family life to make sure their kids show up ready to learn.

item.title: Sewage Spill Reaches Woodbridge, Stafford
item.description: A major upstream sewer line collapse in Maryland has discharged hundreds of millions of gallons of raw sewage into the Potomac River, triggering health advisories for communities, including Woodbridge in Prince William County and Stafford County.

item.title: Supervisor pushes county purchase of former school site
item.description: Occoquan District Supervisor Kenny Boddye says he will introduce a directive for Prince William County to acquire the 96-acre Woodbridge property originally slated for a now-canceled 14th high school.

item.title: Prince William weighs demolition of Bennett School
item.description: Prince William County officials are weighing whether to demolish the historic Bennett School in Manassas as part of a long-planned expansion of the county’s Judicial Center Complex.

item.title: Prince William 311 Marks First Year
item.description: Prince William County leaders say the county’s 3-1-1 service system has handled more than 63,000 interactions in its first year, as officials also prepare to reorganize capital construction under the Department of Transportation.

item.title: Black History Month in Manassas: Honoring Xerk White, the Councilman Who Married Us in His Living Room
item.description: Retired Colonel Ulysses “Xerk” White, the trailblazing first African American member of the Manassas City Council, was publicly honored and celebrated during the City of Manassas’ Black History Month proclamation on February 9, 2026.

item.title: Manassas leaders question county over shared services cost
item.description: Officials in Prince William County, Manassas, and Manassas Park are reconsidering a shared services agreement that has guided regional cooperation for nearly 50 years. Leaders say rising costs and billing concerns prompted the review.

item.title: Code issue forces new home for alt ed program
item.description: A newly launched alternative education program in Manassas relocated before opening after building code restrictions prevented it from operating at the school division’s newly purchased central office.

item.title: Drinking Water Safe After Potomac Spill
item.description: Drinking water in Prince William County, Manassas, Stafford County, and surrounding communities remains safe despite a massive sewage spill into the Potomac River that has triggered health advisories and a federal response.
